<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="ניסן_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918104_theRebbe_982" batchId="meluket-_D7_A0_D7_99_D7_A1_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918104_theRebbe_982__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the Torah is analogous to a human being, composed of a body and soul, corresponding to the commandments and the Torah itself, and that Torah study relates primarily to the soul while fulfilling commandments relates to the body.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And it is written,</t>
    <t s="2">"This is the Torah, a man,"</t>
    <t s="3">that the Torah is in the likeness of a man.</t>
    <t s="4">For just as a man is composed of a body and a soul,</t>
    <t s="5">so too is it in the Torah, which has a body and a soul.</t>
    <t s="6">And in general, this is the distinction between Torah and commandments.</t>
    <t s="7">For the 248 positive commandments are the 248 limbs of the King,</t>
    <t s="8">analogous to the limbs of the body,</t>
    <t s="9">and the Torah is the blood, which is the soul,</t>
    <t s="10">that draws vitality into the limbs of the commandments.</t>
    <t s="11">And this is that the commandments are in time and place, while the Torah is above time and place</t>
    <t s="12">[therefore, anyone who engages in the study of the burnt-offering is as if he offered a burnt-offering,</t>
    <t s="13">even when it is not the time or place of the offering],</t>
    <t s="14">for the body, which is physical, is bounded by time and place,</t>
    <t s="15">while the soul, which is spiritual, is above time and place.</t>
    <t s="16">And just as it is in the Torah and commandments themselves,</t>
    <t s="17">so too is it regarding the connection of the Torah and commandments to the person who studies and fulfills the commandments.</t>
    <t s="18">For the study of Torah relates primarily to the soul, and the fulfillment of commandments to the body.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that although in revelation the Torah is higher than the commandments, in their root the commandments are superior, being G-d's will which is above His wisdom, and the Torah serves as an explanation of the commandments.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it is known</t>
    <t s="1">that this—that the Torah is above the commandments—is as the Torah and commandments are drawn down in revelation,</t>
    <t s="2">but in their root,</t>
    <t s="3">the commandments are more elevated.</t>
    <t s="4">For the Torah is His wisdom, and the commandments are His will,</t>
    <t s="5">will which is above wisdom.</t>
    <t s="6">And moreover,</t>
    <t s="7">even after the Torah and commandments come into the chain of descent, the superiority of the commandments is evident,</t>
    <t s="8">for the Torah is the explanation and elucidation of the commandments.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that similarly, the root of the body is higher than the root of the soul, as G-d's love for Israel through their body stems from His essential free choice, which is above the natural love for their souls.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">From this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="1">that so too is it with the soul and body in man</t>
    <t s="2">[which are analogous to Torah and commandments],</t>
    <t s="3">that although the vitality of the body comes from the soul,</t>
    <t s="4">the root of the body is higher than the root of the soul</t>
    <t s="5">[and as explained elsewhere,</t>
    <t s="6">that the love and connection of the Holy One, blessed be He, to Israel by virtue of their soul,</t>
    <t s="7">"You are children to the L-rd your G-d,"</t>
    <t s="8">is like a natural love, so to speak,</t>
    <t s="9">analogous to the love of a father for his son.</t>
    <t s="10">That is,</t>
    <t s="11">the root of this love is from a level where there is a place for the beloved,</t>
    <t s="12">and it is not from His very Essence.</t>
    <t s="13">However, the love and connection of the Holy One, blessed be He, to Israel by virtue of their body,</t>
    <t s="14">is</t>
    <t s="15">(not due to the virtue of the body,</t>
    <t s="16">nor even the virtue of a son,</t>
    <t s="17">an intrinsic virtue,</t>
    <t s="18">but rather)</t>
    <t s="19">from the fact that the Holy One, blessed be He, chose the body of Israel,</t>
    <t s="20">with free choice,</t>
    <t s="21">and this choice is from His very Essence].</t>
    <t s="22">And this itself—that the soul is drawn to enliven the body—is because of the superiority of the body by virtue of its root</t>
    <t s="23">(in analogy to this, that the Torah explains and elucidates the commandments,</t>
    <t s="24">because the commandments are higher than the Torah).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
